CVX.rationale: Chevron's fundamental health and trajectory are deteriorating sharply. Q1 2026 showed a severe earnings decline: EPS fell 44.5% YoY to $1.11 (from $2.00 in Q1 2025), net income dropped 34.7% YoY, and operating cash flow collapsed 51.6% to just $2.51B. The quarterly trajectory is erratic and incomplete (Q1→Q3→Q2→Q1 pattern with a fiscal gap), making TTM analysis unreliable, but the most recent quarter's results are clearly weak. Gross margin held at 43.2% but operating margin compressed to 9.5% and net margin fell to 5.9%, down from 7.8% a year ago. ROE has declined from 10.5% to 5.9% over the same period. The balance sheet shows rising liabilities ($140.18B vs $106.32B a year ago) while equity grew modestly, suggesting leverage is increasing—likely related to the Hess acquisition integration. Valuation is stretched: the P/E of 30.68 is near the top of its 365-day range (16.7–34.8), having expanded from ~17x a year ago despite deteriorating earnings. The stock is being priced for a recovery that the fundamentals do not yet support. WTI crude has fallen ~27% from its April highs to $73.15, which will further pressure upstream realizations in coming quarters. The Q2 earnings call on July 31 is a potential catalyst, but given the earnings trajectory and oil price headwinds, it is more likely to disappoint than re-rate positively. The Microsoft/Kilby power deal is a long-term positive but won't contribute meaningfully until 2028. Near-term risks include Venezuela exposure, Hess integration execution, and political pressure on oil prices. All three pillars—deteriorating fundamentals, expensive valuation, and unfavorable near-term catalysts—align negatively.
